I am old now, 77 years, and I rent this small piece of land. Maize is our food, so I must try to get fertilizer through the coupon if the chief puts my name — without it we eat poorly. I cannot afford hybrid seed from the shop, so I keep grain from last harvest and plant together with pigeon pea between the rows. My body is tired, so my son and grandchildren help me, and when the ridging time comes I pay one or two men with a little cash or a meal.
